content.title: A Guide to 'The Pitt' Season 2 Cast and Characters
content.text: "Hearst Magazines and Yahoo may earn commission or revenue on some items through these links."Fans can rejoice—HBO Max’s The Pitt is finally back for season two. Similar to the show’s Emmy-winning debut season, the high-stakes medical drama is set at the fictional Pittsburgh emergency medical center—only this time around, it will take place 10 months later during Fourth of July weekend. For the uninitiated, The Pitt is widely celebrated for accurately portraying the adversity and around-the-clock pressure within a modern-day hospital.What sets the series apart is its setup: every episode depicts a 15-hour shift, zooming in on the medical team and their professional—and, at times, personal—conflicts. As for the cast, the show is studded with an ensemble of hard-working characters, including Dr. Michael “Robby” Robinavitch (ER alum Noah Wyle), the chief attendant at Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Hospital’s emergency room. While Dr. Heather Collins (Tracy Ifeachor) has officially exited the series, citing personal reasons, the sophomore installment is still expected to feature fan-favorite faces—plus five new actors are joining the cast in recurring roles. While we count down to the premiere of The Pitt season two on January 8, scroll ahead to get a refresher on the cast and characters who make up the ER.Noah Wyle as Dr. Michael “Robby” RobinavitchNoah Wyle stars as Dr. Michael “Robby” Robinavitch, a senior attending physician who is reeling from the lingering effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. Wyle rose to fame as Dr. John Carter in the NBC medical drama ER. He also appeared in Pirates of Silicon Valley, The Librarian franchise, and Falling Skies.Warrick PageShawn Hatosy as Dr. Jack AbbotShawn Hatosy makes his return to season two as Dr. Jack Abbot, a night-shift attending physician and longtime friend of Dr. Robby. Hatosy is best known for his roles in In & Out, Anywhere but Here, and Animal Kingdom.Warrick PageSupriya Ganesh as Dr. Samira MohanSupriya Ganesh plays Dr. Samira Mohan, a third-year medical resident who has difficulty juggling diligence and speed in the ER. Ganesh previously appeared in shows such as Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago Med, and Grownish.Warrick PageFiona Dourif as Dr. Cassie McKayFiona Dourif portrays Dr. Cassie McKay, a 42-year-old second-year resident and a single mother. Dourif is known for starring in the Child’s Play franchise. She also has roles in True Blood, The Purge, and The Blacklist.Warrick PageTaylor Dearden as Dr. Melissa “Mel” KingTaylor Dearden plays Dr. Melissa “Mel” King, a neurodivergent second-year resident new to the ER. Dearden previously appeared in Sweet/Vicious and American Vandal.HBOShabana Azeez as Victoria JavadiShabana Azeez plays Victoria Javadi, a 20-year-old third-year medical student whose parents are well-respected doctors at the hospital. Before her role in The Pitt, the actor appeared in a number of Australian shows and films, including Run Rabbit Run, Birdeater, and In Limbo.Warrick PageIsa Briones as Dr. Trinity SantosIsa Briones portrays Dr. Trinity Santos, an overly ambitious intern at the ER who is expected to get promoted to a second-year resident in season two. The English actor previously starred in Star Trek: Picard and the Disney+ adaptation of Goosebumps.Warrick PageGerran Howell as Dennis WhitakerGerran Howell plays Dennis Whitaker, a fourth-year medical student. The Welsh actor kicked off his career in the British series Young Dracula. He most recently appeared in Catch-22, Ludwig, and Out There.HBOKen Kirby as Dr. John ShenKen Kirby is returning to the series as Dr. John Shen, a night-shift senior attending physician. The Canadian actor and screenwriter has previously appeared in Good Trouble, Dynasty, and Famous in Love.Warrick PagePatrick Ball as Dr. Frank LangdonPatrick Ball plays Dr. Frank Langdon, a fourth-year resident and Dr. Robby’s protégé. His appearance in The Pitt is his first main television role.Warrick PageKatherine LaNasa as Dana EvansKatherine LaNasa portrays Dana Evans, a sharp-witted and well-respected charge nurse at the ER with decades of experience. The Emmy-winning actor has starred in projects including The Campaign, Truth Be Told, and Deception.Warrick PageLucas Iverson as JamesLucas Iverson is slated to have a recurring role as James, a fourth-year medical student. The American actor’s past projects include I Am Here, Love: Augmented, and Boys Night.Warrick PageSepideh Moafi as Dr. Baran Al-HashimiSepideh Moafi is joining season two as a series regular. Moafi is playing Dr. Baran Al-Hashimi, a new attending physician at the Pitt. The Iranian-American actor gained prominence for her roles in The Deuce, The L Word: Generation Q, and Black Bird.Warrick PageIrene Choi as JoyIrene Choi is set to play Joy, a third-year medical student who is said to have “strong boundaries and a vast knowledge of medicine that leans toward the macabre.”Choi has previously appeared in Insatiable, Good Girls, and The Good Doctor.Warrick PageLaëtitia Hollard as EmmaLaëtitia Hollard joins the cast as Emma, a recent nursing school graduate who, at times, can be considered naïve. The Pitt is Hollard’s first main television appearance.Warrick PageYou Might Also Like
